items.title: Quincy Jones — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: The Road Less Traveled – M. Scott Peck, right? – he says – he starts the book: life is a struggle.

ctx.x: No. So you just learn how to just let it happen and be strong enough, because you know, The Road Less Traveled – M. Scott Peck, right? – he says – he starts the book: life is a struggle. As soon as you accept that, it’s going to get easier. To learn – Basie said the same thing. He says, “Youngblood, it’s about hills and valleys. Anybody can handle the hills.” That’s a metaphor for success. The valleys are the ones that will test you as a human being.

Because when I was looking back through and seeing, like two years before Roots came along, you were already talking about this, and how many of these other things? Like for instance, Soul Bossa Nova. Who in the hell else is going to put two piccolos over the top of a band? Or the thing you said that happened quite by accident, of a flute player coming in . . .
